- `<chunk-size-in-hex>;chunk-signature=<signature>\r\n`

Based on my analysis of the issue, I can see the problem clearly.

The issue is that when a request uses `STREAMING-AWS4-HMAC-SHA256-PAYLOAD` (AWS chunked transfer encoding), the `check_content_md5` function in `s3_listener.py` computes the MD5 hash on the raw chunked-encoded request body, rather than on the decoded payload. The `Content-MD5` header sent by the client was computed on the original (decoded) content, causing a mismatch and the `BadDigest` error.

The `data` variable at line 1228 contains the raw chunked request body (e.g., 320 bytes), while `x-amz-decoded-content-length` header shows the actual content is only 147 bytes. The `Content-MD5` was computed on the 147 bytes of actual content, but `check_content_md5` computes it on all 320 bytes of chunked data.

The fix needs to be in the `check_content_md5` function (or its call site in `forward_request`) to decode the chunked data when the `x-amz-content-sha256` header is `STREAMING-AWS4-HMAC-SHA256-PAYLOAD` before computing the MD5 hash.
